title: Pull a suction stopper out of a basin's drain from under the faucet's spout and put it in the soap dish
instruction: Take the stopper out of the basin's drain and put it in the soap dish.
context: Taking the plug out of a basin, to let the water out or to clean the drain, is something almost everyone does. A grid drain has no plug of its own, so it is closed with a flat suction stopper, which sticks to the glaze. Getting it out takes a firm pull on a small knob at the bottom of a deep bowl, past the faucet's spout, and a grip that keeps hold when the seal suddenly lets go; people with weak hands often find it hard. The stopper is put in the soap dish so it's at hand to close the drain again. The basin is empty, so a real trial stays dry.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the counter (x forward, y left); the layout is the same in every trial. (1) A round white glazed-ceramic vessel basin, fixed: 40.6 across, 14 tall, 1.2 walls, straight sides, a flat inner floor 1.5 above the counter; centred at x 25, y 0. In the middle of its floor, a 4.4 (1 3/4 in) chrome grid drain, which has no plug; no overflow. The drain body passes through a hole in the counter to a standard tailpiece and a water-filled P-trap below. (2) A grey silicone suction stopper, 45 g: a disc 7.5 across and 0.6 thick with a shallow suction cup underneath, and a knob 2.4 across and 2.2 tall in its middle; it is pressed down centred over the drain. (3) A chrome single-lever vessel faucet (a tall basin mixer), fixed, behind the basin: a 5.5 x 5.5 x 1 base plate and a 3.5 x 3.5 square column 30 tall at x 49, y 0, with a lever on top; a 2.2 x 2.2 square spout reaches 20 from the column's axis toward the arms, its outlet 22 above the counter at x 29, y 0 (4 behind the drain, 8 above the rim), so its end is over the back edge of the stopper. (4) A blue-grey ceramic soap dish, fixed with putty: 14 x 11 outside and 2 tall, walls 0.6, centred at x 22, y -30, its long side along x.
scoring: Judged at the end, with a tape measure and the trial video. 'In the basin' means the stopper's middle is within 19.6 of the basin's centre (inside its wall) and under 16 above the counter; 'in the soap dish' means its middle is inside the dish's inner walls and under 4.5 above the counter, in any orientation. 0: the stopper is still sealed on the drain. 0.25: its seal has been broken (some point of its rim came 3 mm or more off the basin floor, or its centre moved 15.5 mm or more off the drain's: lifted, tipped or slid off) but it is in the basin, or it has fallen off the counter. 0.5: the seal is broken and it is anywhere else that isn't the soap dish (on the counter, on the rim or the faucet, held in the air). 0.75: it is in the soap dish but a gripper's fingertip centre is within 6 cm of its middle, or it is still moving. 1.0: it is in the soap dish, both grippers' fingertips are 6 cm or more from its middle, and it has moved under 2 mm in the last 0.5 s, held for 2 s; the trial then ends. A broken seal stays broken: setting the stopper back on the drain later doesn't take the 0.25 away. In a real trial, a stopper still on the drain at the end counts as broken if a luggage scale lifts it with under 2 N, or if the video shows its rim 3 mm up or the stopper 15.5 mm off the drain at any point.
reset_notes: Wipe the drain area and the stopper's underside with a damp cloth, centre the stopper over the drain and press its knob down firmly for 2 s. Check the seal with a luggage scale on a cord loop round the knob's base: a straight pull of 8 to 12 N should lift it. If it reads lower, wipe it wetter and press harder; if higher, press more lightly; if it stays outside the band, replace the stopper. Press it down again. Empty the soap dish.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (Isaac Sim/PhysX, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control). Suction is a 10 N force pulling the stopper onto the floor while sealed; the seal breaks for good once its rim is 3 mm up anywhere or its centre 15.5 mm off the drain. The silicone is rigid, so its edge can't be peeled up alone. The basin is a 32-sided straight-walled bowl with a flat floor; no water. Friction: stopper 1.0, glaze 0.5. The 10 N is an estimate, matched in the real build by the reset check.
